Package com.github.jpmsilva.jsystemd.spring.autoconfigure

Class SystemdSpringApplicationRunListener

java.lang.Object
com.github.jpmsilva.jsystemd.spring.autoconfigure.SystemdSpringApplicationRunListener
All Implemented Interfaces:
SpringApplicationRunListener, Ordered
public class SystemdSpringApplicationRunListener extends Object implements SpringApplicationRunListener, Ordered
A Spring Application Run Listener that sets up the integration with systemd, as early as possible during the startup of the application.

Once the environment is prepared, it configures the Systemd instance and logs the integration status, and sets up an ApplicationRunStatusProvider to provide status updates of the current phase of the application life cycle. Once the application context is prepared, it registers a bean that closes the instance when the context is closed, and sets up an ApplicationContextStatusProvider to report the bean creation progress. Once the application has started, it tells systemd that the application is ready, if so configured with systemd.ready-event=application-started, rather than once it accepts traffic. If the application fails, systemd is told why, and the instance is closed.

Applications that configure the instance themselves depend on jsystemd-spring-boot rather than the starter.

Nothing is set up in the applications that Spring Cloud runs next to the actual application (see the "Application hierarchies" page of the documentation).

Author:
Joao Silva

  • Field Details

    • ORDER

      public static final int ORDER
      The order of this listener. It must run after Spring Boot's EventPublishingRunListener (order 0), which initializes logging when the environment is prepared, so that the systemd integration status can be logged. It is kept away from Ordered.LOWEST_PRECEDENCE so that other listeners can still be ordered after it.

    • failed

      public void failed(@Nullable ConfigurableApplicationContext context, Throwable exception)
      Tells systemd why the application failed, with the most specific cause of the failure, as the status the service unit is left with, and closes the instance, as the context may not have created the bean yet, in which case it would not close it. The reason is the last status sent, so that the status providers that report the shutdown do not replace it while Spring Boot closes the context, which it does after calling this. When the refresh of the context fails, the context destroys its beans before, closing the instance, which can still send the reason, as it is sent directly.
      Specified by:
      failed in interface SpringApplicationRunListener
